summary: A person in a take replaced cut by cut from a reference portrait, the rest of the take and its soundtrack kept.
description: Replace one performer across a multi-cut take with a referenced identity, keeping the background, lighting, camera, performance and the take's own soundtrack. Prepare with replace-performer-cuts (it writes `cuts` and the person mask), then pass source_video, mask_video and cuts here. Each cut is trimmed from the source and the mask, held to its render_frames (on the 17n + 5 grid, 124 to 345), regenerated inside the mask by an H3 ref2va regional edit at refine_strength 1.0 with the cut's own audio held, cut back to its num_frames, and the cuts are joined hard (no crossfade) before the whole source track is paired back on. A cut carrying `seed` renders with it, else the workflow `seed`; re-roll one cut by rerunning with only that cut's seed changed. A cut carrying `prompt` renders with it, else the workflow `prompt`: give each cut whose framing or cast differs its own prompt describing that cut's pose, action and framing, because the edit redraws the person from the prompt and a prompt written for another cut redraws the wrong pose. Two people in the take, one replaced: run the prep with track=2, look at its people-contact_sheet.png to see which number is which person, and pass output:<prep workflow identity>/<run id>/final/people-person-2.mp4 as mask_video; only person-2 is regenerated. Numbering is per cut, largest first, so check each cut. Limits, each refused before the run: 1 to 32 cuts (for_each's); each cut's render_frames on the 17n + 5 grid inside 124 to 345 and at least its num_frames; references within the ref2va class's limits, at most 9 images and 12 files in all; source and mask the same size and 24 fps.

vram_estimate.reason: regional-edit's estimate per cut - the swap step renders num_frames = the cut's render_frames, with its source and mask clips as guides (bytes_per_guide_voxel) - plus music-video's per-reference term, since ref2va keeps each reference's encoding resident (#1374)

variables.prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the man in <Picture 1>, early 60s, short greying dark hair, round wire-rimmed glasses, a full grey-and-dark beard, wearing a mustard corduroy jacket over a dark green crew-neck t-shirt.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is one close-up shot of a 1990s multi-camera sitcom: <Subject 1> answers an accusation without looking up from his magazine, in front of a live studio audience.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the face, glasses, beard, hair, corduroy jacket and proportions of <Picture 1> are kept exactly, with the head and jaw newly animated to speak; the grey studio backdrop of <Picture 1> is not used.

detailed_description:
The target video is in the style of a 1990s multi-camera sitcom, shot on studio video with warm, even, shadowless lighting. [Shot 1] A medium close-up frames <Subject 1> from the chest up, seated at the end of an olive-green couch in front of a brick wall, holding an open magazine just below the frame line and reading it, his glasses low on his nose. He does not look up. <Subject 1> (S1), a flat, low, unhurried male baritone voice, completely unbothered, says <d>[English] Technically? The freezer has a defrost cycle.</d> On the last word he turns a page. A live studio audience laughs as the line lands. The camera holds a static close-up throughout, the way a sitcom cross-shot camera holds a speaker.

overall_soundscape:
A bright, close television-studio room tone. A soft page turn, the faint creak of couch springs as <Subject 1> settles, and a rolling wave of live studio-audience laughter that starts on the last word of the line and carries under the end of the shot.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

render_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps; a cut's render_frames is what H3 renders for it, so it must be on that grid, with no 'snap' since detect_cuts already wrote the grid's value

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
